title: Position: Insights from Survey Methodology can Improve Training Data

bias_targets.methodology: Theoretical evaluation drawing on survey methodology to conceptualize how an annotator's propensity to participate correlates with their demographic characteristics and subjective labeling decisions, leading to unrepresentative training data.

Theoretical evaluation using social science survey models to explain how the sequence in which data instances are presented alters annotator perception and subsequent labeling outcomes (e.g., contrast and assimilation effects).

Reviewing psychological and survey literature to hypothesize how providing pre-labeled suggestions causes annotators to over-rely on the suggestions and fail to correct errors (also referred to as automation bias).
Evaluating how overly relying on common examples provided in annotation guidelines or instructions can cause labelers to omit or mislabel less common items.

Applying cognitive miser theories from survey methodology to evaluate how labelers take mental shortcuts (e.g., straightlining, acquiescence, or failing to read instructions) when faced with cognitively demanding or repetitive labeling tasks.
